title: Gerunds & Infinitives
summary: Some verbs are followed by gerunds (-ing), others by infinitives (to + verb), and some by both.

theory.markdown:
After some verbs, use a **gerund** (verb + **-ing**).
After others, use a **to-infinitive** (to + base verb).

**Verbs + gerund**: enjoy, finish, avoid, keep, suggest, practise, consider, mind, miss, admit, deny
*I enjoy **cooking**. / She finished **reading**.*

**Verbs + infinitive**: want, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, agree, refuse, manage, offer, forget
*I want **to eat**. / She decided **to leave**.*

**Verbs + either** (no change in meaning): like, love, hate, prefer, begin, start, continue
*I like **swimming**. / I like **to swim**.*

**Verbs + either** (change in meaning):
- *I **remember locking** the door.* (I have a memory of doing it)
- *I **remembered to lock** the door.* (I didn't forget to do it)

items.source: He decided to change his job.
I don't mind waiting — take your time.
items.translation: Nie przeszkadza mi czekanie — nie spiesz sie.

exercises.prompt: They decided ___ (move) to a bigger flat.
I finished ___ the report an hour ago.

exercises.sentence: He suggested to go to the cinema.
answers: He suggested going to the cinema.
She refused to take part in the meeting.
She refused to attend the meeting.

exercises.prompt: He keeps ___ (interrupt) me when I'm talking.
She managed ___ the exam on her first attempt.

exercises.sentence: I hope seeing you at the party.
answers: I hope to see you at the party.
I forgot to book a table.
I forgot to reserve a table.

exercises.sentence: I enjoy to watch old films at the weekend.
answers: I enjoy watching old films at the weekend.

exercises.source: Planuja kupic nowy dom w przyszlym roku.
answers: They plan to buy a new house next year.
They are planning to buy a new house next year.
